chat.text: https://notes.ietf.org/notes-ietf-127-regext looks empty ?

chat.text: these docs both got published today

chat.author: Mohamed Boucadair
chat.text: Indeed, Gavin.;

chat.author: Jim Reid
chat.text: Why do 5 have to say yes? How many of them must be called Jim? :grinning:

chat.author: Roger Carney
chat.text: :slight_smile:

chat.author: James Galvin
chat.text: @tim Hmm, not expecting that.  Let me copy the agenda into the notepad.

chat.author: James Galvin
chat.text: Thanks Gavin and Med.  Both documents published today.  Yeah!

chat.author: James Galvin
chat.text: @Jim - 5 is a number we came up with like 10 years ago.  We are a small group and we generally seek unanimity among our key participants.  5 is a number that gets us there.  And, we always take any objection very seriously.

chat.author: Roger Carney
chat.text: 3915bis as is, Gould comments should be rolled into RGP2

chat.author: Jody Kolker
chat.text: +1 Bill.

chat.author: Karl Dyson
chat.text: We should just address the errata in this doc, fix the error in RGP2 per Gavin's comments about not breaking server operators.

chat.author: Karthik
chat.text: @Jimgalvin, Thanks!

chat.author: Gavin Brown
chat.text: thanks Jim!

chat.author: Roger Carney
chat.text: Thanks Gould!

chat.author: Gavin Brown
chat.text: @Maarten: RFC 10026 says that automation SHOULD NOT be disabled in the presence of a registry lock

chat.author: James Gould
chat.text: I don't believe locking needs to be manual.

chat.author: Maarten Wullink
chat.text: yes, for dnssec this may be, but csync is something else

chat.author: James Galvin
chat.text: I believe that the actual purpose of registry lock and what it protects should be a matter of policy.  Whether or not it should be manual depends on what you are trying to protect.

chat.author: James Galvin
chat.text: My comment was about the “Security Considerations” not fully describing the security issues.

chat.author: Paweł Kowalik
chat.text: one more argument to remove these registrations from -extensions draft

chat.author: Roger Carney
chat.text: @James, I agree that Registry Lock should be dictated by Registry Policy

chat.author: Paweł Kowalik
chat.text: +1 Roger / James.

chat.author: Jim Reid
chat.text: Can exactly 1 registry lock work for >1 registry policies?

chat.author: Jody Kolker
chat.text: +1 Roger/James Also.

chat.author: Roger Carney
chat.text: @Reid (too many Jims), if I am understanding your question correctly, I would think so

chat.author: Mario Loffredo
chat.text: @Chairs Do you think that, similarly to documents ready for WGLC, priority should be given to discuss documents that aim to be adopted ?

chat.author: James Galvin
chat.text: @mario - we have not considered prioritizing new work.  It is worth noting that we have a few documents already on a list to be adopted and we are perhaps adding a number of documents to that list.  I would say our default will be first-come first-served. What would working group members prefer?

chat.author: Jim Reid
chat.text: I'd prefer some triage on priorities rather than FCFS.

chat.author: Gavin Brown
chat.text: lowering my hand as Jim answered my question :)

chat.author: Suzanne Woolf
chat.text: +1 Jim, prioritizing is hard though-- anything besides FCFS can be misunderstood or misapplied.

chat.author: Suzanne Woolf
chat.text: (disambiguating: that was addressed to Jim Reid, not Jim Galvin)

chat.author: James Galvin
chat.text: What the chairs can do is make visible the list as we have it.  That way WG members can make their concerns visible and we’ll address those comments.

chat.author: Jim Reid
chat.text: @Suzanne, it may be hard but can be necessary. It'll be bad if something "important" can't get adopted because the WG's in-tray is jammed up with not so important IDs

chat.author: Barbara Bellis
chat.text: Sorry, was struggling with the camera. The status sets maps to our model, we have many different types of locks set by the registry. The one question I have about registry lock specifically is adding it can come with a cost, and so a fees extension type mechanism is needed to tell registrars how much it cost and check they know what they'll be paying.

chat.author: Mario Loffredo
chat.text: Last time I asked for adotion of draft-loffredo-regext-rdap-verified-contacts, I was told that the policy was adopting new documents as documents drop off our list. Is this the right time to ask for its adoption ?

chat.author: James Galvin
chat.text: @mario yes, and noted.

chat.author: Mario Loffredo
chat.text: Thanks a lot Jim

chat.author: Suzanne Woolf
chat.text: @Jim I can think of at least one WG whose chairs attempted such an assessment; they were accused of trying to "bring voting to the IETF". It's just meant it can be tricky out there :-)

chat.author: Suzanne Woolf
chat.text: Sorry, "I just meant..."

chat.author: James Galvin
chat.text: @barbara - thanks for the comment.  I suggest you send a note the list so the point is not lost.  Thanks.

chat.author: Barbara Bellis
chat.text: thanks @james, I will do that.

chat.author: James Gould
chat.text: For Barbara, the use of the status set extension for a locking service, which uses client statuses that are authorized by status set instead of server statuses, can include the support for the registry fee extension for fees.

chat.author: Jim Reid
chat.text: I agree Suzanne. But there's no need for "votes". IMO we can rely on the infinitely wise co-chairs to decide what is and isn't important/urgent.

chat.author: Jim Reid
chat.text: Joe, how much interest have registrars shown in this?
